issues.claim: Начиная с .NET 8 ASP.NET Core публикует гистограмму `http.server.request.duration` (meter `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting`) с атрибутом `http.response.status_code`
issues.problem: I know this claim is true, so it is not an unsure issue. The fetched excerpt is only the entry page, and it redirected to the aspnetcore-11.0 version. It shows the metric name and the meter but not the .NET 8 start version or the status-code attribute.
issues.suggestedFix: Link the HTTP metrics reference page of the ASP.NET Core built-in metrics docs, which lists the attributes. Optionally set meta.dotnetVersion to "10" because the answer depends on the runtime version.

issues.claim: Какую долю месячного бюджета ошибок съедает пятиминутный всплеск, а какую - доля ошибок 0,5%, которая держится неделю?

issues.suggestedFix: Optional: shorten it to a single question about how much of the monthly budget the fixed-threshold alert actually protects, and mirror the change in EN.

issues.problem: The linked, current messaging-spans page uses `messaging.system.name` (Required), and the excerpt shows it. `messaging.system` is the older name. The answer tells the candidate that attribute names changed between versions, but then gives the outdated name without naming a convention version. A candidate would learn the wrong attribute.
issues.suggestedFix: Write `messaging.system.name` (older conventions: `messaging.system`) and `messaging.destination.name`, in both ru and en. Optionally name the convention version at the point where it says to pin it.
